items.note: The focused filter field keeps its 1px ink border and adds a pink halo and an ink ring, beside the outline status pills and a single result row with a pink flag. It reads clearly and in the reference's drawn-ink language, but the clear glyph inside the field is drawn in blue, outside the reference's ink-only chrome.

The focus treatment carries over correctly: an ink border, a pink halo and a white ring on a black field. The page reverses the reference's dark depth, though. The ground is charcoal and the panels are pure black, so the boxes sink instead of sitting a step above a black ground as in the reference's dark capture.

The lemon header band, stacked ink-framed stat boxes and the pink-haloed focused filter read like the reference's phone app screen. Two samples let the primary pill nav run off the right edge instead of collapsing into a menu button, and the table's status column is cut off at the box edge.

An ink-framed table on paper: a header row, 1px ruled rows, outline status pills with colored dots, and a notched pink flag in each budget cell. The rows are read-only, so the hover shows no change, which follows the spec. The table has the hairline character of the reference's filter stack.

The same ruled table and pink flags appear on black panels over a charcoal ground. The structure holds, but the inverted ground and panel tones flatten the separation that the reference's black ground gives.

The table stays in its ink frame and scrolls horizontally, below the band and the stacked stat boxes, in the system's language. In one sample the first column is so narrow that names break one word per line, and the status pills are clipped at the frame edge.

Focus on a nav pill draws a 2px ink ring at an offset around the pill, both on the black current pill and on a plain item. It is crisp and unmistakable, matching the reference's keyboard-focus outline.
The ring turns white around the white current pill and reads clearly, like the reference's dark nav. The surrounding page again uses a charcoal ground with black boxes, the reverse of the reference.

The ink ring around the focused nav pill or menu button is clear on a phone. As on the other phone screens, two samples keep a pill nav row that runs off the screen edge instead of collapsing into the menu button.

The menu is a white panel with a 1px ink frame and a static hard ink shadow. A ruled header row holds the email in meta grey, and plain rows follow. It looks like a picked-up paper cutout, exactly the reference's lift language.

The menu becomes a black panel with a light hairline and ruled header, but its hard shadow almost disappears against the charcoal ground. The panel-darker-than-page inversion makes it read as a hole rather than a lifted sheet.
On a phone, a wide white menu with an ink frame and hard shadow drops over the band, and its rows are large and legible. In one sample the email in the menu header breaks mid-word onto a second line.

A dashed white box on paper holds an ink-outlined drawn object (a folder or a slip) in a band color, one sentence, a helper line and a clear-filters action. This is the reference's dashed empty state, raised by a proper sticker instead of a glyph.

The empty state carries over with its dashed box and colored sticker, and in one sample a pink action. It sits on a black panel inside a charcoal ground, so the dashed box loses contrast compared with the reference's dark treatment.

The dashed empty box stacks under the focused filter with an ink-outlined object, the message and a full-size action. It follows the reference's phone empty state closely and is each sample's own drawing.

The stat tiles become dashed white placeholder boxes at their final size with visible "Loading" text, as the recipe asks. The busy refresh button greys out its fill and label in two samples. That reads as disabled rather than as the reference's ink-and-white button with a small working glyph.
The dashed placeholders on black panels and the "Loading" text are clear. The busy button turns light grey on the lemon band, and the inverted ground and panel tones weaken the frames.
Full-width dashed placeholder boxes with "Loading" text stack under the band and are well drawn. The busy button is again a flat grey slab with a blurred glyph in two samples.

The chart follows its recipe: grey bars with ink caps, a pink average line with ink-outlined dots, and dot legends. Each sample draws its own parcel sticker with an ink outline and a thin side band, but it is about 80px, shoved into the top-right corner and cropped by the band's top seam. It reads as a fragment, far from the reference's big, deliberate die-cut objects.

Only the header sticker carries motion: a scroll-linked ft-drift that stays still without scrolling. The bands are static. This matches the spec and the reference's restraint, where only the stickers move.

findings.summary: The header-band sticker is still a small corner fragment. It is about 80px, pinned into the band's top-right corner and cropped by the top seam as well as the side, so only part of a parcel shows. The reference places its objects deliberately: big, mostly visible, cropped by one edge, so each reads as a whole die-cut object.
findings.promptFix: A header-band sticker sits vertically centred at the band's trailing edge, at least as tall as the band's title block, and is cropped by one edge only (the side), never by the band's top or bottom seam. At least 60% of it shows on every viewport. If the band is too short, shrink the sticker rather than pushing it into the corner.

findings.summary: In dark mode the ground is charcoal and the panels, menus and placeholders are pure black, the reverse of the reference's black ground with lighter boxes. Panels sink, menu shadows vanish and dashed boxes lose contrast. The spec's dark tokens set this up, and they are unchanged since the last review.
findings.promptFix: Dark mode: the page ground (`color.surface.default`) is black and raised boxes (`color.surface.raised`) are one step lighter (#242423), edged with the light hairline. Lifted menus and dialogs keep a visible hard shadow against that ground.

findings.summary: The busy button turns into a flat grey slab with grey text and a smudged glyph, which reads as disabled. The reference's buttons never go grey: the label and ink frame stay and only a small working glyph changes.
The clear glyph in the focused filter field is still drawn in blue, a colored icon in the ink-only chrome.

On phones the primary pill nav runs off the right edge instead of collapsing into the menu button. The scrolling table's first column breaks names one word per line, and status pills are clipped at the frame.
The email in the user menu header breaks mid-word, leaving a single letter on its own line.
